The directions stay in view on a narrow window

Every picture is the real Plan page (Mobile), photographed, with the proposal drawn into the live page.

1 · Today

Below 1200px the directions go across the top. Scroll down and they scroll away. Only the open direction's title stays, so switching means scrolling back up.

And on a narrower window the last direction runs off the end of the strip.

2 · Proposed: only the strip stays

The strip sticks under the top bar. The open direction is filled navy, the same as the Plan button above it, and the other directions are greyed. So its title does not need to stay as well: it scrolls away with the plan. Any direction is one click away, wherever you are on the page.

3 · Squeezed, the names wrap

When a name does not fit on one line it wraps onto a second, or a third on the narrowest window. Names are never cut, and every direction stays on the strip. Pointing at a greyed direction darkens it.

4 · While editing

The same strip, with the reorder handles on the line and + Add a Pillar at its end. Done editing is already in the top bar, so the title scrolls away here too.

5 · At the top of the page

Before scrolling it is the same strip. When the names fit, the code sits beside the name on one line instead of above it, so the plan starts a little higher than today.

What changes

Only on a narrow window
Above 1200px the side list stays exactly as it is, with the title held at the top beside it, as today.
The title
On a narrow window it scrolls away with the plan, reading or editing. The same goes for a project's title on Capabilities.
What it costs
About the same room for the plan as today once you scroll: 4 to 10px more when the names take one or two lines, 13px less when one needs three. At the top of the page, up to 22px more.
A unit with many directions
Up to ten fit on the strip even at the narrowest window. With that many, a long name that needs more than three lines ends in “…”, and pointing at it shows the whole name. Past ten, the strip scrolls sideways.
